findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category or uncategorized_category_id has no row in site_settings.
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. `site_settings` only stores values that were changed from their defaults. If `embed_category` was never set, or its name matches no category, the result is empty, `[0]` raises, and the migration aborts during deploy. The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same problem. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing, and fall back to a safe default.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized or escaped, so existing embeds break, and the old settings are deleted anyway.
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` setting allowed entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`; the old specs used exactly these. The migration inserts each line raw. It skips the model's scheme and path stripping and does not remove whitespace or `\r`. `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` with `lower(host)`, so those rows never match, and embedding stops working for those sites. A value containing `'` also breaks the SQL statement. Line 31 then deletes the original settings in a `change` migration with no `down`, so the data cannot be recovered. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank lines, quote values with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`, and make the delete reversible or keep the old setting values.

findings.title: update and destroy return a 500 for an unknown id.
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError. This happens, for example, when two admins delete the same host. Use `find` or `raise Discourse::NotFound` so the client gets a 404.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil.
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises when `host` is nil, for example when the admin API receives `embeddable_host[category_id]` without `host`. The result is a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the normalization with `if host.present?`, or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port or uppercase letters never match.
findings.body: The validation accepts `host:port`, and `before_validation` does not strip the port. `uri.host` never includes the port, so a host saved as `example.com:8080` is never allowed. The column is lowercased in the comparison but the referer host is not, and the stored value is not downcased. Downcase both sides and strip or compare the port consistently.

findings.title: A delete failure is silently ignored.
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the server delete fails, the admin sees no error and the row stays as if nothing happened. Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, as `save` does.
